extra.message: User input from request.form.get('username') and request.form.get('password') is interpolated directly into an SQL query string using an f-string and passed to cursor.execute(). This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL such as ' OR 1=1 -- to bypass authentication.
The admin credentials (USERNAME='admin', PASSWORD='password123') are hardcoded as plaintext string literals in the source code. Anyone with access to the source can obtain privileged credentials.

The value of request.args.get('q') is interpolated directly into an HTML response via an f-string with no escaping. An attacker can craft a URL like /search?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers.

The session cookie value (user) is interpolated directly into an HTML f-string response at line 47 with no escaping. An attacker can set this cookie via the XSS payloads on /login (username field) or /search (q param) and execute JavaScript on /dashboard.

The string literal '<script>alert('XSS Vulnerability!')</script>' is hardcoded into the response at line 47, guaranteeing that any visitor to /dashboard will have this script executed in their browser.

The /dashboard route has no authentication or authorization check. The comment on line 45 confirms this: '# No authentication check'. Any unauthenticated user can access the dashboard by navigating directly to /dashboard, bypassing the login flow. Only a default cookie value of 'guest' is read, but the cookie is not verified.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Session is managed via a simple cookie set with set_cookie('session', username) at line 38. The cookie value is the raw username (untrusted input) with no cryptographic signing, no expiration, no HttpOnly flag, no Secure flag, and no SameSite attribute. This allows trivial cookie forgery and session hijacking.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: The /login endpoint returns different responses for valid vs invalid credentials: a 302 redirect for success (line 37-39) vs a 200 text response for failure (line 41). This differential allows an attacker to enumerate valid usernames without knowing the password, and enables automated credential-stuffing attacks.
